By building a habit of contributing what we can, we aim to foster the Jesuit value of service to others. The 1634 Society also seeks to celebrate traditions here at Georgetown. By hosting a number of signature events on campus each year, including Traditions Day, a component of Homecoming Weekend, we help keep the history of Georgetown alive with each new class. description: We, the Abolition Advocacy Project (AAP), are law students advocating, empowering local movements, and educating fellow law students at Georgetown University Law Center to abolish systemic injustices on which Washington, D.C., and United States legal institutions are built and perpetuate. We aim to challenge the status quo, integrate abolitionist aims into our legal education, and engage with the broader DMV community through coalition building, collaboration, and grassroots organizing. Georgetown students face many pressures and difficulties, and this club intends to connect students to resources and educational materials.

description: The ABCS is composed of seven undergraduate student members who are appointed by the outgoing Advisory Board. ABCS supervises the overall administration and effectiveness of Club Sports. The Advisory Board for Club Sports advises those Club Sports teams that have access to benefits and determines which new clubs will be granted access to benefits under University policy. ABCS funds and develops policy for the governance of all Club Sports under its jurisdiction.

description: AASV combats sexual violence and rape culture through education, advocacy, and systemic reform. The organization is committed to inclusiveness and recognizes that sexual violence is a communal harm. Students in AASV examine the legal and social underpinning of sexual violence and rape culture, shifting and encouraging discourse around gender roles, coercion, and consent in Georgetown University Law Center and the broader law community.

name: Africa Forum
description: Our mission is to spread awareness and promote dialogue about the 54 nations of Africa amongst Georgetown University graduate students.

name: African Society of Georgetown
description: The African Society of Georgetown University (ASG) is a student organization that seeks to affirm, educate and cultivate a community of students affiliated or interested in Africa's various cultures.

We are committed to advancing justice in DC. description: The Alternative Breaks Program (ABP) brings together Georgetown community members in order to foster intersectional solidarity and inspire lasting commitments to service and social justice. ABP trips engage with diverse and vibrant communities through direct service, immersion, and reflection in a substance-free environment. By creating a space for sustained dialogue and action, ABP strives to build long-term relationships with community partners and bring the experience home.

Students chosen to join Barristers' Council begin intensive training to represent Georgetown Law at national and international advocacy competitions.

description: Big Buddies is a student organization sponsored through SFS where we have a group of Georgetown graduate students from across the university who meet once a month to do fun activities and bond with a group of elementary school kids from Key Elementary in Arlington, VA.

description: BMDT is a faculty-directed, academic for-credit class. This contemporary modern dance theatre company was founded over 25 years ago by African American women with an artistic vision and passion to express the African American experience through dance. Our company strives to help dancers from all walks of life to express their experiences through dance.

name: Black Perspectives on Public Policy
description: BPoPP’s mission is to provide a safe space for Black-identifying graduate students to discuss policies that affect the Black community. BPoPP intends to cover a wide array of policy issues to ensure that Black voices are heard in all social and political spaces. At the same time, BPoPP aims to connect individuals across diverse backgrounds and policy interests by serving as a tool for all students to better understand how policy and politics affect their Black counterparts.

name: Black Student Alliance
description: We, the Black Students of Georgetown University, conscious of the educational, political, cultural, social, and spiritual deficiencies at said university, do hereby come together to be hereafter known as the Black Student Alliance. We form this group for the purposes of cultivating a community of joy and with the aim of reconciling the deficiencies of this PWI with the safety, support, reaffirming pride, self awareness of unapologetic Blackness by infusing the student experience with Black culture. We exist in the security of our resilience!

name: Black Theatre Ensemble
description: We, the Black Theatre Ensemble, appreciate the theatrical, performative, and technical talents of artists devoted to portraying and enriching the Black cultural heritage throughout the dramatic arts. Black Theatre Ensemble to produce works of Black artists and/or works relating to the experiences of the Black community. description: The Campus Ministry Student Forum (CMSF) is an assembly responsible for supporting and advocating for undergraduate Campus Ministry student organizations at Georgetown. The Forum works with an elected Executive Committee to allocate Student Activities Fee funding, advocate for the needs of Campus Ministry student organizations, and bring student-led groups together to improve collaboration and cooperation. description: The mission of Georgetown University Campus Recreation at Yates Field House and Kehoe Field is to provide the Georgetown campus and surrounding community with fun, inclusive, engaging, and educational fitness and wellness programming that promotes personal growth and the development of lifelong skill sets.

description: The CALL is an innovative undergraduate program situated at Georgetown University's Capitol Campus. Georgetown University students will have the extraordinary opportunity to immerse themselves in downtown living for a full semester, soaking in the vibrancy of Washington, D.C.; engage in meticulously curated courses that embody the ethos of experiential learning, led by esteemed Georgetown Faculty and seasoned practitioner; cultivate fresh conn

description: "CCC" is established for the expressed purpose of developing cultural awareness of Caribbean roots and culture and to encourage students of all ethnic backgrounds to explore and experience the Caribbean heritage.

name: Catholic Women at Georgetown
description: Committed to prayer and outreach, we engage life on the Hilltop—and beyond—with joy and creativity. Aware of the pressing mission of women in our time, we journey with Mary, our model and Mother, offering a sense of sisterhood to all women of faith on campus. As Catholic Daughters, we seek to create a sisterhood of Catholic women centered around service and spiritual development. Curious? We always welcome new faces! Please contact catholicwomen@georgetown.edu with any questions or concerns that you may have about the recruitment process.

description: The Advisory Board for Student Organizations (ABSO) is an advisory and funding board of the Center for Social Justice that works to support the missions of student organizations under the CSJ's purview. The board is composed of 10-16 students with a staff ex-officio advisor. ABSO oversees, facilitates, and provides resources to student-run social justice service activities, student advocacy, and community involvement activities at Georgetown. ABSO is responsible for advising student organization leaders on programming and budgeting, and serves as a resource for understanding university policy.

name: Center for Social Justice Graduate Interns
Center for Social Justice Operations Team
description: The Operations Team supports CSJ EngageDCorps programs, student organizations, community-based learning courses, engaged research, and racial justice work through "behind-the-scenes" infrastructure and logistics. Members of the Center Operations Team will work closely with CSJ professional staff in necessary administrative and financial work, training and compliance, and other operations. Hours for each Operations team member are highly flexible and built around that student's schedule. The Operations team includes opportunities for leadership development.

name: Center for Social Justice Research, Teaching & Service
description: The Center for Social Justice Research, Teaching, and Service (CSJ) opened its doors in 2001. Our vision is collective liberation: a world in which we all live with dignity and determine our futures in just community. The CSJ transforms education and interrupts systems of oppression. Our work centers community knowledge, critical reflection, and the redistribution of resources.

name: Center for Student Engagement
description: The CSE fosters campus-wide engagement and student development by working with campus partners and undergraduate students in a Jesuit context. name: Chinese Student Association
description: The Chinese Student Alliance (CSA) has a two-fold mission: first, we seek to create an inclusive and welcoming environment where students can find a community, as well as explore Chinese culture and language. Second, we hope to further cross-cultural exchange and understanding by highlighting diverse cultures and traditions in Chinese and Chinese American communities. We also hope to engage students in insightful discussions on social, political, economic, and cultural issues related to China and Chinese Americans.

description: The Georgetown University Chinese Students & Scholars Association(GUCSSA) as a student-led organization strives to improve the lives of Chinese Students in Georgetown University(GU) by advocating for student needs and engaging students in systemwide, state, and federal higher education policymaking.

name: Circle of Indigenous Students Alliance
description: CISA is a group of dedicated Native Americans and allies interested in discussing and promoting tribal affairs, culture, and policies affecting Native American communities. We participate in political, health care, education, cultural, and community service activities throughout DC to further our organization's goals.

name: Classical Studies Club
description: The Georgetown University Classical Studies Club is focused on serving as a community for Georgetown students and faculty interested in discussing, debating, and learning more about classical societies.

name: Club Field Hockey
description: Our mission is to create an environment for students to develop their field hockey skills and stay active while also building a sense of community and providing an outlet for students to exercise and play field hockey on a competitive yet fun level.

name: Corporate & Financial Law Organization
description: The purpose of the Georgetown Corporate & Financial Law Organization ("CFLO" or "the Organization") shall be to provide a forum for Georgetown University Law Center ("GULC") students and alumni interested in meeting and discussing current topics in corporate and financial law and to provide CFLO members with access to experienced practitioners, members of academia, professional organizations, and fellow students to facilitate professional competence and career advancement.

name: Corporate Crime & Anti-Corruption Law Students Association
description: The purpose of the Corporate Crime & Anti-Corruption Law Students Association (CCAC) is to create a forum for students to pursue their interests in the field of corporate crime and anti-corruption. CCAC’s vision is to create opportunities for Georgetown University Law Center students and alumni to engage with different areas of the law related to financial crimes, including but not limited to corporate compliance, anti-money laundering, government enforcement, asset recovery, counter-terrorism financing, white-collar defense, Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, bribery, and internal investigations.

name: Council of Advisory Boards
description: The Council of Advisory Boards hosts the semesterly club fair as well as administers the new club development process. CAB works to advocate on behalf of all student organizations with access to benefits in order to best represent their common needs and encourage collaboration.

description: DC Schools Project (DCSP) is a tutoring, mentoring, and advocacy program that engages Georgetown students as volunteer and Federal Work Study (FWS)-funded tutors to provide English language tutoring and support for youth and adults of immigrant backgrounds in Washington, DC. description: DCivitas envisions a world in which nonprofits have access to the resources and business strategies they need, allowing them to fully devote themselves to serving their respective communities. Ultimately, DCivitas aims to positively impact the D.C. community.

name: Decolonizing International Affairs
description: Decolonizing International Affairs is a graduate student-led organization and network at Georgetown University that studies, discusses, and develops decolonial approaches to our work in global affairs. We work to promote scholarship, practices, and policy in support of self-determination and social justice for indigenous and colonized peoples. name: Dept of Performing Arts
description: Georgetown's Department of Performing Arts (DPA) integrates creative and critical inquiry, emphasizing artistic excellence, interdisciplinary learning, socially engaged performance, and the spirit of collaboration. The department is home to the College's undergraduate degree programs in American Musical Culture and Theater & Performance Studies with dozens of performing groups in all aspects of the performing arts (music, theater, dance and film). name: Detroit Legal Alliance
description: Recognizing the continuing legal challenges faced by indigent populations of Detroit, Michigan and the surrounding areas, DLA shall organize an opportunity for the students of Georgetown University Law Center to serve the most vulnerable of the city during Spring Break. Building upon the well-established relationships with various public interest organizations in the city, DLA shall provide a unique service and travel opportunity outside the District of Columbia. description: The mission of the Disabled Law Students Association is to (i) foster a supportive community for students with disabilities, (ii) advocate for the concerns and needs of the diverse disability community, (iii) promote the success of students with disabilities on campus and beyond through professional development, (iv) bring awareness to non-disabled students about the need for intersectional approaches that are inclusive of the disability community, and (v) advocate for structural, political, and social reforms that acknowledge and respect the aims of disability justice and accessibility within

description: Diversity and Inclusion @ Georgetown (DiG) aims to leverage the diversity of Georgetown's graduate students to create culturally-competent global leaders through skills-based programming in diversity and inclusion-based issues.

For many women in these communities, a lack of access to resources and exposure can hinder their ability to jumpstart their own business ventures. Early Entrepreneurs bridges this gap by utilizing experiential learning to provide young girls with the mentorship and fundamental business education required to embark on their passions for business and in turn also nurtures a community of female entrepreneurs through peer-to-peer mentorship.

name: Economics Graduate Student Organization

name: Environment and History Research Seminar
description: To encourage Georgetown Graduate community to think about environmental issues from a historical perspective. Environmental history provides context essential to link past environmental transformations to present policies and future strategies for a sustainable life. Environmental history helps scholars, researchers, teachers, policy makers, business people make better informed decisions with lessons learned from the past.

name: Equal Justice Foundation
description: The Equal Justice Foundation exists to provide supplemental funding awards to Georgetown University Law students, ensuring no student is financially precluded from pursuing summer legal opportunities in the public sector.

name: ESCAPE
description: ESCAPE is a first-year and transfer retreat program designed to create a space for students to get to know their classmates and engage in conversation about the journey of college. Small groups, led by upper class mentors, foster a sense of meaning and belonging throughout the retreat as well as the rest of your Georgetown career. The retreat is designed as an escape from the Hilltop. ESCAPE is accessible to people of all religious and non-religious backgrounds and reflection is a central part of the retreat experience. name: European Horizons
description: European Horizons is a global, student-led policy incubator whose mission is to give young people a voice in shaping the future of Europe and of transatlantic relations. Through our network of university chapters across the world, and in collaboration with our partner organizations, European Horizons devises, tests, and advocates for innovative policy ideas to advance European integration.

name: Federalist Society
description: The Georgetown University Law Center ("Georgetown Law") student chapter of The Federalist Society is dedicated to the principles that the state exists to preserve the natural law of human freedom; that the separation of governmental powers is central to the U.S. Constitution; that the duty of the federal and state judiciaries is to say what the law is, not what it should be; and that any and all threats to these principles must be vigorously resisted through the means of civic engagement, open debate, intelligent discourse, and generosity of spirit.

name: Filipino Law Association at Georgetown
description: This organization aims to connect Filipino students and those interested in Filipino culture by creating a community on the law campus to serve as a space to celebrate and promote Filipino heritage.

name: First Generation Investors X Georgetown University
description: FGI x Georgetown proactively addresses economic inequality by working with high school students from underserved areas of D.C. Throughout an eight-week financial literacy curriculum, FGI's tutors ensure students master paramount financial concepts such as stocks, bonds, credit, interest, and more. At the end of the eight-week curriculum, candidates receive a $100 portfolio to their name. Students choose their investments within the preset allocation: 70% will go into ETFs, 20% into bond-based funds, and the last 10% into stocks of the student's choosing.

name: First Generation Student Union
description: Georgetown FGSU is the first-generation student group on campus. We aim to pool the energies and creativity of our members to advocate for a Georgetown Law that is more inclusive and comfortable for 1G students. Our primary goal is to help facilitate the transition to law school for first-generation graduates at Georgetown Law by building a supportive community of students, faculty, staff, and alumni.

name: First Year Orientation to Community Involvement
description: First-Year Orientation to Community Involvement (FOCI) is an intensive pre-orientation program for incoming first-year and transfer students. FOCI serves as an introduction to community service, activism, and social justice issues in Washington, DC. FOCI participants actively engage in community service; discover and reflect on the diverse populations, perspectives, and roles that exist in the Georgetown and greater DC communities; develop leadership skills; and become part of a community committed to personal growth through service and reflection. description: Georgetown Foreign Affairs, Science & Technology (FAST) is a graduate student organization focused on bringing people together around issues of science, technology, and international affairs (STIA). Science and technology are transforming all components of international affairs, but they also establish new frameworks and provide new tools to approach the global problems in the 21st century. FAST hopes to promote these issues and deepen STIA knowledge across the Graduate School. name: Georgeown University Students for Health and Medical Equity (GUSHME)

We will accomplish this by addressing social determinants of health through training of cultural awareness and sensitivity programming on campus, with local service partnerships and experiences abroad.

name: Georgetown African Law Society
description: The Georgetown African Law Society exists in recognition of the deep need for a platform on the Georgetown Law campus that centers on the development of Africa and African students. As an association, it is designed to provide an opportunity for Georgetown lawyers and law students of African descent; those with an affinity for the continent, and all with Africa-focused career goals to come together. It is intended to be a space for comradery, networking, knowledge sharing, debate, and care.

name: Georgetown American Civil Liberties Union
description: The ACLU is a nonpartisan student organization that works to protect civil liberties and civil rights through trainings, speaker events, protests, and other forms of advocacy.

name: Georgetown Anti-Poverty Society
description: The Georgetown Anti-Poverty Society (GAPS) is an international development student society. We host forums, panels, workshops, coffee chats, and other events that connect graduate students with a variety of practitioners from the public, private, multilateral, and non-profit sectors. We aim support students' academic and professional development through skill-building, networking, and discussion relating to issues of international development.

name: Georgetown Arabic Department Graduate Association
description: The Georgetown Arabic Department Graduate Association (GADGA) seeks to: a) provide a platform through which graduate students can present their current research projects to fellow students and faculty members, offering a valuable opportunity to receive feedback on their work; b) provide relevant academic training in the field of Arabic & Islamic Studies through faculty and expert-led workshops; and c) provide a welcoming environment for members of GU community who wish to gain more exposure to, and deepen their understanding of, Arabic and Islamic societies and cultures.

If you are interested in joining the team, contact the captains at equestrianclub@georgetown.edu.

Our mission is to increase the understanding of the transatlantic relationship and associated issues in the Georgetown community through discussions with guest speakers, faculty, and club members. description: The Georgetown University Farmers' Market was founded to improve access to and availability of healthy, fresh food on Georgetown's campus. description: GUFC's mission is to encourage members to fully explore the sport of fencing, build character traits such as a sportsmanship, responsibility, and perseverance, and uphold the ideals of Georgetown University.

description: GUGAMS is a neutral, apolitical, lay, and inclusive organization, which objective is to serve the Mexican graduate community at Georgetown by: 1.- Encouraging communication and collaboration across the Mexican community throughout the University. 2.- Recognize issues and concerns affecting the Mexican community and provide ways and means of addressing those issues as efficiently as possible. 3.- Organize events that will bring the GUGAMS community together for professional and academic development, as well as social enjoyment. 4.- Foster relations and encourage communication between the GUGAMS

name: Georgetown University Hellenic Association
description: The Georgetown University Hellenic Association brings together students of various backgrounds; some are international students from Greece, some are Greek-American, some are not ethnically Greek, some speak Greek, some do not - the one thing all Hellenic Association members have in common is a love of Greece and all things Greek! name: Georgetown University Math and Science Hands On Enrichment
description: GUMSHOE's mission is to provide remedial instruction and tutoring in math and science to elementary, middle, and high school students within the DC Public School system. Our organization is comprised on undergraduate and graduate students from Georgetown University who have strong a understanding of the topics in which they tutor. Our goal is to foster not only an understanding of, but also an appreciation for math and the sciences in hopes of narrowing the achievement gap that exists in the DC Public School system. For more information, please email us at GUMSHOE@Georgetown.edu.

name: Georgetown University Men's Club Volleyball
description: Georgetown Men's Volleyball Club is established to create a community for Georgetown students to practice and play volleyball and to represent Georgetown University in local and national competitions.

name: Georgetown University Men's Ultimate
description: Georgetown Men's Ultimate provides all Georgetown University students with the opportunity for intercollegiate and club play in the sport of Ultimate. The organization is responsible for teaching and developing the necessary skills to be competitive in the sport. Georgetown Men's Ultimate strives to produce a competitive and respectful team atmosphere for all members of the organization, consistent with the spirit of the game.

name: Georgetown University Mock Trial
description: Georgetown University Mock Trial is a community of competitors that strives to improve their skills in public speaking, acting, and debate.

name: Georgetown University Moot Court Team
description: Moot Court emulates appellate court proceedings in the form of inter-collegiate competition. Together we prepare and argue a case in front of a panel of judges as well as write an accompanying legal brief.

name: Georgetown University Mosaic
description: Mosaic is dedicated to representing and empowering multiracial and multiethnic students. To that end, Mosaic provides a space for all to embrace their culture and history and develops a community for multiracial/multiethnic students on Georgetown's campus. Mosaic builds community through bonding, educational, and discussion events.

name: Georgetown University Museum Society
description: To foster an appreciation for the arts, history, and culture among Georgetown students, and to build an on-campus community through off-campus exploration of institutions of art, culture, and history.

name: Georgetown University National Association for the Advancement of Colored People Chapter
description: The mission of the NAACP is to ensure the political, educational, social and economic equality of rights for all persons and to eliminate racial hatred and racial discrimination. At Georgetown, the vision of the GU NAACP chapter is to build and empower our community by raising awareness and consciousness of contemporary issues, activism, service, and increasing political efficacy. Through dialogue, events, community bonding and healing, we hope to work towards liberation by wholly meeting the needs of students of color.

name: Georgetown University Oncology Patient Support
description: GUOPS aims to provide an artistic outlet to patients and visitors of the Lombardi Cancer Center in conjunction with the Arts and Humanities Department by encouraging creativity and wellness through arts and crafts activities. In achieving this mission, GUOPS hopes to help volunteers develop empathy, communication skills, and an awareness of the responsibility to participate and work in the health sector.

name: Georgetown University Pep Band
description: The Georgetown University Pep Band is an organization of Georgetown students dedicated to supporting Georgetown Athletics & University events through musical performance. Founded in 1922 as both an ROTC (which became the Pep Band) and a Concert Band (which became the Concert Winds and then the Wind Ensemble). Members support the arts by sharing their enjoyment of music with audiences and fans alike at athletic events, official and unofficial university events and functions, and occasionally at non-university, off-campus events.

name: Georgetown University Pre-Law Society
description: The Georgetown Pre-Law Society provides undergraduate students with the opportunity to learn about law school and its admissions process. In addition, we aim to share law-related news and career opportunities through events, mentorship, and community-led discussion.

name: Georgetown University Pre-Medical Society

name: Georgetown University Right to Life
description: Georgetown University Right to Life (RTL) is a student organization dedicated to protecting human life from conception to natural death. We strongly believe in the value of all human lives, no matter who they are, no matter where they live — even if they are living in the womb. Through persistent effort, we can and will create a society in which abortion, euthanasia, the death penalty, and all assaults on innocent human life have no place. A society in which the sanctity and dignity of each human life is valued and defended.

name: Georgetown University Rugby Football Club
description: Georgetown University Rugby Football Club is a no-cut team that seeks to provide an opportunity for any individual to learn a new sport, find a community, and have fun. We emphasize camaraderie and personal growth with opportunities to play at every skill level. Whether you are a life long rugby player or do not know the rules, we encourage you to join us in representing Georgetown on the rugby field!

name: Georgetown University Softball Club

description: At Georgetown University Technology and Engineering Club (GUTEC), we are united by our shared interest in using technology and engineering principles to solve problems small and large. We welcome students of all experience levels to participate in our events and projects. GUTEC aims to provide opportunities for everyone to grow in efficient teamwork and engineering skills. description: Teach In plans and implements lessons on civics, basic legal principles, and careers in the law for DMV-area middle school and high school students. Our organization provides a unique opportunity for Georgetown Law students to pass on their knowledge and expertise to the next generation of aspiring lawyers. Teach In facilitates interactions that deepen DC-area students' understanding of the legal profession and legal careers while simultaneously encouraging Georgetown students to connect to the community in which they live.

name: GUSA
description: The mission of the Georgetown University Student Association (GUSA) is to empower Hoyas by giving them control over resources, improve the quality of student life, safeguard student rights, involve students in the governance of the University, and ensure that the University conducts itself in an ethical and responsible manner.

description: Health Education Services (HES) is the primary campus provider of health education, and seeks to promote the health and well being of all students through care for the WHOLE Hoya: body, mind, and soul. name: Health Law Society
description: Health Law Society aims to educate Georgetown Law students about opportunities in health law and connect students to practitioners in the field.

name: Hoya Hub
description: The Hoya Hub food pantry is a resource for any member of the Georgetown University community experiencing food insecurity. It is a pantry stocked with non-perishable food items, available to anyone who needs food on an immediate, emergency basis. No Hoya should go hungry; the Hoya Hub is a place to pick up nutritious food to cover short breaks or other unplanned gaps in access to meals.

name: Hoya Knits
description: Hoya Knits is committed to giving back to the larger DC community through donations of handmade baby and children’s hats that are knit by our very own Georgetown community. This organization provides students with the opportunity to learn knitting skills in a collaborative, low-stress environment and the space to relieve stress and anxiety in a productive and enjoyable manner. These handmade hats are then donated to various hospitals and shelters in the DC area.

name: Hoya Lawya Runners
description: The purpose of Hoya Lawya Runners shall be to: 1. Provide a forum for runners of all levels to participate in organized and non-organized runs and races. 2. Educate members on the benefits and joys of running and fitness generally. 3. Educate members on proper methods of running as a means of reducing injury and maximizing individual health and wellness. 4. name: Hoya Saxa Weekend
description: Each spring, the Center for Multicultural Equity & Access (CMEA) hosts Hoya Saxa Weekend in partnership with the Office of Undergraduate Admissions. Hoya Saxa Weekend is a chance for underrepresented students of color to experience campus life, meet current students, and have important questions answered before making their college decision. CMEA is excited to bring potential Georgetown students of color to campus in a celebration of what the University has to offer. Hoya Saxa Weekend is also run in conjunction with the Georgetown Admissions Amabassador Program (GAAP).

name: Hoya Taxa
description: Hoya Taxa is a student volunteer organization that promotes financial literacy and assists lower-income D.C. families with their taxes. Each year, club members are trained to receive IRS certification as volunteer tax preparers, then travel to clinics in the D.C. area to help clients file their tax returns. Hoya Taxa, which operates through the Center for Social Justice, is partnered with Community Tax Aid D.C., the non-profit that operates these tax clinics and offers free income tax preparation services.

name: HoyAlytics

This club (Hoyalytics) would satisfy this need by (1) providing a service to fellow Hoyas in demonstrating and informing students of various aspects of data analytics and (2) establishing networking opportunities and career outreach with MBA students and leading executives.

name: Hoyarn

name: Hoyas For Immigrant Rights
description: Hoyas For Immigrant Rights (HFIR) is a community at Georgetown University committed to dialogue and service for immigrant rights. HFIR fosters informed and respectful conversation about immigration and immigrant rights and forms a network of individuals dedicated to action and advocacy. Our purpose is to empower students, promote awareness, build brave and safe spaces, and serve as advocates and liaisons for immigrant students in our campus and the community.

name: Hoyas for Recovery
description: The mission of the Hoyas for Recovery (HFR) group is to advocate for policies and programs that promote the academic and social well-being of recovering students, faculty, and staff at Georgetown University through the praxis of social justice, service, empowerment, and community building. We seek to help establish a supportive atmosphere on campus for students, faculty, and staff, who are in recovery from a substance use disorder (SUD) and persons who are affected by another person's SUD.

description: The Initiative on Catholic Social Thought and Public Life is a unique effort to promote dialogue on Catholic social thought and national and global issues, build bridges across political, religious, and ideological lines, and encourage a new generation of Catholic lay leaders to see their faith as an asset in pursuing the common good.

name: Innovo Consulting
description: Innovo Consulting is a student-run consulting group at Georgetown University that provides pro-bono advisory services to social impact startups and nonprofits. We work with a mix of student entrepreneurs and community members while also offering career development and educational opportunities to the Georgetown student body. From incorporating a business to restructuring one or from launching a marketing campaign to managing finances, our student consultants can help a venture take the next step to success.

name: International Refugee Assistance Project at Georgetown Law
description: The International Refugee Assistance Project (IRAP) organizes law students and lawyers to develop and enforce a set of legal and human rights for refugees and displaced persons. Mobilizing direct legal aid, litigation, and systemic advocacy, IRAP serves the world's most persecuted individuals and empowers the next generation of human rights leaders. The Georgetown Law Chapter works to support that mission. Visit our site for more info on IRAP, how to get involved and to sign up for our newsletter: https://irapgeorgetownlaw.org/

name: International Student Assoc.
description: ISA's mission is to foster a greater unity within the international student community through a social network based upon the common experience of studying abroad in the United States, promote greater diversity and international awareness in the university community, and create a forum for international students to voice their distinctive concerns and interests.

name: International Students Association
description: This Association intends to bring together international students from our diverse student body and integrate them into the Georgetown Law community. By providing adequate support through mentoring schemes and socials, we hope that international students can settle into their new lives in the U.S. with relative ease and start taking advantage of all that Georgetown Law has to offer. name: Iranian Cultural Society
description: The Iranian Cultural Society is dedicated to promoting interest in and understanding of Iranian culture in the Georgetown community. ICS is non-religious, non-political, and open to anyone who is interested in Iran and the greater Persian world.

name: J. Reuben Clark Law Society
description: We affirm the strength brought to the law by a lawyer's personal religious conviction. We strive through public service and professional excellence to promote fairness and virtue founded upon the rule of law.

name: Japan Dialogue Forum
description: The Japan Dialogue Forum was established to facilitate graduate students in the School of Foreign Service, the larger Georgetown University community, and those interested in Japan in discussing, sharing expertise, and contributing to the overall national and international dialogue about U.S.-Japan relations and Japanese foreign policy in an open forum. Through the Japan Dialogue Forum, members will join a network of others in the Japan foreign policy and relations space to connect, discuss, and keep Japan within the focus of ever-shifting national and international interests.

name: Japan Network
description: The Japan Network is established for the purpose of increasing awareness of the country of Japan, its people, and its society. Japan Network shall undertake several cultural projects each academic year. We seek not only to increase student awareness of Japan, but also to represent an organization in which native Japanese students may find a forum for voicing common concerns and interests in the Georgetown community, and where students of any background may gain exposure to Japanese culture.

name: Japanese Law Association at Georgetown
description: 1. To diversify and enrich the Georgetown University Law Center community 2. To promote cultural exchange among students at Georgetown Law 3. To promote Japanese culture, customs, heritages, and traditions in order to support the Japanese legal, academic, and professional studies at Georgetown Law; 4. To fully commit, collaborate, and cooperate with Georgetown Law administration and any other student organizations to prosper such great opportunities

name: Jewish Graduate Student Association
description: The Jewish Graduate Student Association (JGSA) at Georgetown University is committed to fostering an inclusive, welcoming, and empowering community for Jewish graduate students from diverse backgrounds and perspectives. Our mission is to celebrate Jewish identity through cultural, spiritual, educational, and social programming; to promote leadership and dialogue within and beyond the Jewish community; and to enrich the Georgetown graduate experience by building meaningful connections on campus and across the greater D.C. Jewish landscape.

name: Jewish Law Students Association
description: The Jewish Law Students Association (JLSA) is a community outlet and organization for Jewish students of all backgrounds and beliefs at Georgetown University Law Center. Our presence on campus aims to foster our members' expression and exploration of their Jewish identities personally, professionally, culturally, and spiritually. By offering engaging and meaningful JLSA programming and by connecting students with other Jewish organizations and alumni, we contribute to the wellbeing of Jewish students at the Law Center, the broader Georgetown community, and the D.C. Jewish community in which we

name: Jewish Student Association
description: The Jewish Student Association plans programs and activities for Georgetown's pluralistic Jewish community and, working with the Office of Campus Ministry, makes sure regular religious services, study sessions, and other activities are made available to students and to all members of the Jewish community at Georgetown. As an entirely student-led organization, the JSA provides students with the opportunity to form an active part of their own Jewish life on campus. Students lead religious services, organize activities, and help steer the Jewish community at Georgetown. The JSA also works closely

description: Guided by the Jewish value B’tzelem Elohim, or literally in the image of G-d, we form this group to create a space for Jewish students to build community and advocate for peace, justice, and human rights. We establish this group in the shadow of the horrific violence of the last month. description: Members of Justice and Diversity in Action (JDA) strive to create and sustain an environment that supports each other's work for social change and commitment to grow in knowledge of human diversity in all its aspects. Together, we seek to be open, honest, and sensitive in examining attitudes, prejudices, and actions that undermine respect for diversity and perpetuate injustice, as these arise both within and beyond the Georgetown University community. description: This organization's purpose shall be to promote diversity at the Law Center by supporting and representing the voices of Korean American law students and its friends.

name: Korean Student Association
description: The purpose of the Georgetown University Korean Student Association is a. To promote diversity by sharing Korean culture with the greater Georgetown community, b. To establish a safe community for Korean international students who are away from home, c. To bridge the gap between Korean international and Korean American students, d. To support the relationship between past and current members of the organization.

name: La Casa Latina
description: La Casa Latina is a centralized location of inclusivity in which Latinx students can share their narratives, access resources integral to success on the Hilltop, and engage in vital discussions about the intersectionality of race/ethnicity, class, sexuality, gender, ability, privilege and power within the Latinx identity. In order to unite all members of the Latinx community, Casa Latina will ensure that students feel not only welcomed at Georgetown, but also feel empowered to grow and flourish in all encompassing aspects of the collegiate community.

Latin American Foreign Affairs Association

These events will open the door for meaningful engagement with matters connected to the history, people, culture, and current events of the region.

description: LALSA's main purpose is to address the needs and well-being of Latino students at GULC by providing a welcoming environment in which students feel comfortable and can thrive. An equally important purpose is to connect Latino students at GULC with the surrounding legal and the greater Hispanic communities. We accomplish this through our three organizational pillars: community outreach, professional development, and social events.

name: Latin American Student Associa
description: The Latin American Student Association (LASA) brings together students of all Latin American backgrounds, identities, intersections, or simply interested in Latin American culture to build a strong and supportive community on campus, create opportunities for professional development and leadership, advocate for their shared interests, and give back through service to both local communities in the DMV area and communities across Latin America.

name: LATINERG
description: The LatinERG will seek to provide tangible support at Georgetown University where Latine employees and allies will share, develop and thrive through community to build a formal, collective voice that is heard by leadership, resulting in enhanced cultural awareness, inclusivity, employee engagement, and effective systemic change-making. Through our different faiths, cultures, and beliefs, we will commit to being a diverse space that values commitment to justice and embodying cura personalis – a profound care and responsibility for one another.

name: Latter-day Saints Student Association
description: Recognizing the many choices that confront students attending the Georgetown University, the Latter-day Saints Student Association (LDSSA) is established to help students have a balanced secular and spiritual educational experience during their years of formal education. The LDSSA exists to create and maintain a positive, supportive, and inclusive community for LDS students on campus, as well as students interested in learning more about the LDS faith and religious practices.

name: Lattes & Lit Book Club
description: As gathering places aimed at fostering community engagement and open dialogue at Georgetown, the Library and the Midnight Mug would like to create a book club open to the entire Georgetown community. The book club will provide an opportunity for people from across campus to come together to discuss themes relevant to our community and explore diverse viewpoints. FOR INFORMATION ABOUT THE GROUP AND TITLES WE'RE READING, VISIT THE LATTES AND LIT WEBSITE: https://guides.library.georgetown.edu/lattesandlit/ Goals and Objectives Build community: Bring book lovers together from across campus to disc

description: Law and Political Economy (LPE) is a growing movement to cultivate legal thinking rooted in the insight that politics and the economy cannot be separated - both are constructed in essential respects by the law. It can be understood as a critique and alternative to the orthodox Law and Economics scholarship, which centers economic "efficiency" and lacks frameworks for thinking systematically about the interrelationships between political and economic power. description: LSDAD is a non-partisan student organization which aims to galvanize law students to defend democracy and the rule of law. LSDAD’s focus is on action. Through pro bono work, publishing materials on democracy and the rule of law online, hosting events for pro-democracy speakers and organizations, and other measures, LSDAD aims to organize law students in defense of democracy. Lawyers and law students have unique positions and duties in American society. description: LSCA activates and mobilizes the power of law students to transform the legal industry's role from exacerbating climate injustice to meaningfully supporting a just transition. We aspire to move legal ethics and practice towards a just transition for our climate, in solidarity with frontline communities, to build an equitable and sustainable world in our lifetimes. name: Leaders in Education About Diversity
description: Leaders in Education About Diversity (LEAD) is a dynamic peer education and leadership development program; through facilitation of open dialogue, LEADers seek to educate themselves and others about diversity and intersections of identity in order to build common ground across the Georgetown University community.

Lebanese Student Association

Through community, solidarity, and cultural celebration, we strive to advocate for our shared interests, foster a vibrant Lebanese cultural presence on campus, and give back to local Lebanese communities and to communities across Lebanon.

name: Legacy of a Dream Internship
description: Together, Georgetown University's Office of Government Relations and Community Engagement (GRACE), Office of Student Employment, and Center for Social Justice announce a pilot program through which Federal Work Study (FWS)-eligible Georgetown University undergraduate students can intern with DC-based community organizations whose leaders have been recognized by the University's annual John Thompson, Jr. Legacy of a Dream Award. name: LGBTQ Center
description: The Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer, and Questioning (LGBTQ) Resource Center provides education, programming, support services, and voice to Georgetown students, faculty, staff, and alumni of all sexual orientations and gender identities. We are committed to understanding sexual orientation and gender identity in the context of and as it intersects with race, religion, ethnicity, nationality, ability, socio-economic status, and culture. Our mission is to strengthen connections across cohorts, foster mentorship between alumni and students, and provide a platform for networking, collaboration, and professional growth. description: The mission of Lombardi Ensemble Association for Patients (LEAP) is to create a therapeutic environment for Lombardi Cancer Center patients, families, and hospital staff through musical performances. Our volunteer organization consists of musicians who strive to create a comfortable and supportive environment for the patients while growing together as students in musical creativity and ability. description: The Georgetown University chapter of the Make - A - Wish Foundation operates in unison with the parent organization to fulfill the wishes of children across the country battling life - threatening illnesses. Through organizing & hosting events within Georgetown's campus and local community, MAWGU members apply fundraising, marketing, and management skills to raise both money & awareness for Wish kids desperately in need of a spark of hope during their medical battle.

name: Mask and Bauble Dramatic Society
description: Mask and Bauble Dramatic Society is the oldest continuously running student theatre group in the country, currently celebrating our 174th season. Mask and Bauble (M&B) is dedicated to creating quality theatre through a tradition of student-to-student mentorship. With an aim to produce a wide variety of works each season, our show selections also draw from our three pillars of classics, musicals, and student written works. Visit maskandbauble.org for more information!

name: McCourt Energy & Environmental Policy
description: Section 1: Mission The McCourt Energy & Environmental Policy group seeks to build a Georgetown community for energy and environmental policy by engaging students, academics, and practitioners on these policy topics.

name: McDonough Student Advisory Board
description: The board’s vision is to support the McDonough School of Business in creating diverse, innovative, and inclusive environments for all students who seek to find professional development and belonging among their peers. By providing guidance and resources to clubs, the board aims to foster learning, career development, leadership, philanthropy, innovation, and camaraderie to positively impact the Georgetown community and greater world.

name: McDonough Student Body Government
description: We serve as representatives of the undergraduate business student body, working with the undergraduate dean's office on curricular concerns and opportunities, as well as broader community-building activities, including service work and Jesuit values-centric events.

name: McDonough Women
description: McDonough Women seeks to foster a community of individuals who share the goal of empowering undergraduate females to pursue careers in business. We host a variety of unique events and workshops that provide professional growth opportunities and incorporate mentorship and peer collaboration. Additionally, McDonough Women collaborates with top firms to organize networking opportunities for members.

name: Men's Club Lacrosse
description: The GUMCLT is established for the purpose of enjoying the sport of men's lacrosse in a fun and competitive atmosphere. Men may join regardless of their ability level.

name: Men's Club Squash
description: The Georgetown Men's Squash Club looks to provide a competitive squash environment for the school's best players. Students in the Club will have the opportunity to represent Georgetown University in the collegiate squash community; to train and receive professional coaching multiple times per week; and to have the opportunity to travel and compete. The Club seeks to foster comradery, wellbeing, and personal development through sport.

name: Men's Club Water Polo
description: A competitive club water polo team that competes against other colleges up and down the East Coast. We are a strong group of athletes and strive to build even stronger relationships within our team. Consistent finisher at the top of our league.

name: Men's Ice Hockey Club
description: A competitive environment in which high school, prep school, and junior hockey players can continue their hockey careers at the college club level.

name: Methods Lab
description: Methods Lab is a "laboratory" established to build an inclusive community of neuroimagers; expand opportunities to exchange ideas, share code, receive feedback, and learn new research methods through journal club discussions, workshops, and hackathons; and foster a culture of open psychological science and cognitive neuroscience at Georgetown University and in the greater Washington DC area.

name: Middle Eastern and North African Law Students Association
description: The mission of Georgetown Law's Middle Eastern and North African Law Student Association (MELSA) is to provide a healthy and accepting cultural platform for law students of Middle Eastern and North African descent. The organization's main purpose is twofold: (1) to promote diversity and inclusion on campus and in the greater community via outreach efforts, and (2) to provide student members with a welcoming network where they can thrive and connect with the greater Middle Eastern and North African student body and community.

name: Military and Veterans Resource Center
description: Georgetown University is proud to serve those who have served our country. Our office serves to support the opportunities of military members accessing higher education to ensure a campus culture that cares for the entire spectrum of military-connected students. The mission of our services is to instill the Jesuit spirit of cura personalis into everyday connections among the military-connected community. description: The National Security Law Society (NSLS) aims to utilize Georgetown Law's existing strengths in the national security field and works to further develop Georgetown Law's reputation as an academic leader. The NSLS seeks to create a network of JD and LLM students interested in national security law and to connect them with professors, mentors, and experts in the field.

description: The members of NALSA reach out to support students of Georgetown University Law Center who have tribal affiliations, grew up nearer Indian Country, or would like to support and work with tribal issues or communities, or in Indian Country. Members will be leaders for Native American rights and issues. description: Founded in 1982, nomadictheatre is one of Georgetown University's premier co-curricular student theatre groups. Since its inception, Nomadic has committed itself to creating theatre that is both technically ambitious and socially engaged. In that spirit, Nomadic pushes its designers and actors alike to create innovative productions that take artistic risks and feature challenging themes.

name: Office of Campus Ministry
description: Guided by Georgetown's Catholic and Jesuit tradition, with its abiding commitment to interreligious collaboration, Campus Ministry equips students to lead lives of deeper meaning, belonging, and purpose.

name: Office of Global Services

name: Office of Neighborhood Life
description: The Office of Neighborhood Life supports all students, non-students, and permanent residents in the communities surrounding Georgetown University. Our office will educate students about university policies and local ordinances; continue to build and strengthen neighborhood relations by facilitating dialogue; and promote civic citizenship to create a positive quality of life for everyone living in the neighborhood.

name: Office of Residential Living
description: Mission Create comfortable, inclusive communities that foster formation and engagement. Vision Innovative Space, Integrative Learning, Dynamic Communities Values Care, Faith & Justice, Inclusivity, Learning, Service, Student Ownership

description: The Office of Student Conduct supports Georgetown University’s Catholic and Jesuit educational mission by enforcing regulations designed to promote an environment in which students can develop intellectually, morally, spiritually and socially while exercising a balance of partnership and autonomy within the campus community. name: Office of the Student Ombuds

name: Orthodox Christian Fellowship
description: A chapter of the North American OCF where students and faculty of all different Orthodox denominations, and anyone interested in learning more, can be part of a close-knit community.

name: Outdoor Education
description: Through wilderness based endeavors, Georgetown University Outdoor Education seeks to teach, to inspire, and guide students, creating a community where learning, personal challenge, reflection, and increased compassion for others and the environment are fostered and upheld as core values.

name: Outlaw
description: The purpose of Outlaw is to promote LGBTQIA equality, to educate the Georgetown University Law Center community on issues affecting LGBTQIA people, and to create a welcoming social environment for LGBTQIA students and their allies at the Georgetown University Law Center.

name: Parliamentary Debate Team
description: Officially founded in 2013, Georgetown Parliamentary Debate has established itself in the American Parliamentary Debate Association league, finishing 7th in the nation as a university in 2018 and 4th in the nation in 2019. A Georgetown team also won the prestigious Team of the Year (TOTY) award with impressive finishes at tournaments throughout the year. With a new officer and member core, we are ready to travel and compete intensely in the 2019-2020 season. We will be hosting a tournament at Georgetown in the spring, and will continue to bring the enrichment that accompanies academic debate.

name: People's Parity Project
description: People's Parity Project (PPP) is a movement of law students and attorneys organizing for a democratized legal system which empowers working people and opposes subordination in any form. Together, PPP seeks to dismantle a profession that upholds corporate power and build in its place a legal system that reflects the values of justice, equity, and solidarity. We aim to educate and raise awareness of present and future opportunities to build from abroad a stronger, safer, and more dynamic Colombia. Our organization strives to engage people of Colombian background together with those of other nationalities, in the task of improving Colombia's image to the rest of the world, showcasing the country's improvements over the past decade. We aim to provide an atmosphere in which LGBTQ+ individuals can develop and strengthen a sense of pride, self-worth, awareness, and belonging in the community. Project Lighthouse provides an accessible resource for Hoyas to anonymously and confidentially voice their concerns to a sympathetic ear. Our volunteers donate their time to create and deliver programs to pediatric patients at the MedStar Georgetown University Hospital. We also hold craft kit making sessions and fundraising for the national Project Sunshine organization. Our goal is to relieve the anxiety of the young patients and create an environment of positivity and fun while they are receiving care.

name: Rangila
description: For 32 years, Rangila has been Georgetown University's flagship cultural tradition. Organized by Georgetown's South Asian Society, Rangila is the largest charity dance showcase in the country. This year's showcase will feature over 450 performers, 14 genre and fusion dances, and Georgetown's only South Asian musical group. Rangila 32 is partnering with the Solar Water Project to bring sustainable clean water infrastructure to communities in need in Swat Valley, Pakistan. Every dollar of Rangila's proceeds will go towards this incredible cause.

name: Refugee Pulse Initiative
description: Refugee Pulse Initiative's Community Outreach Program is dedicated to empowering refugee populations with the life-saving skill of CPR. RPI has established partnerships with community centers and foundations throughout the DMV to offer CPR courses tailored to the specific needs of these communities. The program goes beyond language barriers by providing courses in multiple languages and employing instructors who are not only socially and culturally educated but also deeply passionate about serving the refugee populations.

name: Ritmo y Sabor

name: Rotaract Club of Georgetown University
description: The Rotaract Club of Georgetown University aims to bring together friends, leaders, and problem-solvers who wish to create lasting change – across the globe, in our communities, and in ourselves. Through commitment and vision, we strive to channel our passion and energy to take action on our world's most persistent issues. Join us in our mission to provide service, promote integrity and advance world understanding, goodwill, and peace through our fellowship of engaged leaders, committed to doing what is in our reach to make the world a better place.

name: SABRE: Student Advisory Board of Real Estate
description: As an organization, we value human connection and professional development. SABRE bridges the gap between academic study, industry knowledge, and social interaction. Our core values center around fostering meaningful connections between individuals and facilitating the development of their professional skills. name: Science Policy Network

Through various professional, social, and educational events, we strive to familiarize our members with the world of policy. GSPN will foster the skills necessary to successfully advocate and participate in policymaking for scientific research, innovation, and literacy. description: The Senior Class Committee (SCC) of Georgetown University is led by a board of ten students with the goal of producing a memorable last year at Georgetown by exposing seniors to culturally diverse experiences, charitable services, and transitional activities geared towards post collegiate life. The Senior Class Committee plans the major Senior social events including Disorientation, Senior Homecoming, Senior Parents Weekend, Senior Auction, Senior Ball, and Senior Week. description: The SFSAC is the elected representative organization of the SFS undergraduate population. As advocates for the SFS student body, the SFSAC collaborates with the Dean's Office, the Georgetown University Student Association, and the other academic councils to address issues pertaining to academic affairs, the student body in the SFS, and other initiatives developed to enhance the undergraduate experience. Originally a network of business students and professionals who desired to add a social sector element to their work, Net Impact has grown into an interdisciplinary network bringing together business, design thinking, and start-up exercises to drive social and environmental change. description: The mission of the Georgetown University Sikh Student Association is to communicate and allow participation in three major tenets of Sikh life; Simran (religious events), Seva (community service), and Sangat (social and cultural events) for Sikh students on campus. The SSA will also function to provide Sikh and non-Sikh students with the opportunity to engage tangibly with Sikh religious traditions and practices via student-led programming at on and off-campus venues. description: The Association aims to improve the academic and social lives of SJD Scholars through: (a) A supportive and collaborative network of scholars; (b) Adopting and furthering the Association's positions on academic and student life matters; and (c) Engaging with Faculty and Administration to address academic and social issues.

name: Slow Food Georgetown
description: Slow Food aims to broaden the Georgetown student body's awareness of the importance of universal access to food that is good, clean, and fair. To us, good food is made with love and the intent to build community and bring sustenance; clean food is produced with respect for the environment and the health of those who consume it; and fair food is recognized as the result of the labor of many who deserve just compensation and equal access to food themselves, and recognizing and standing up to the violence that often accompanies food production. name: Smart Woman Securities
description: Georgetown Smart Woman Securities is a chapter of the national organization sponsored by Warren Buffett. Our organization provides weekly educational seminars, hosts exclusive recruiting events, and facilitates an environment to meet new people with common interests. The goal of Smart Woman Securities is to support women in their social, professional, and educational goals.

name: SNUGS at Georgetown
description: Our mission is to organize accessible swim instruction specifically designed for children with special needs in the greater DC community. The swim lessons aim to prevent accidental drowning, which is among the leading causes of death for children with intellectual disabilities. In addition to promoting water safety, SNUGS at Georgetown will create an inclusive social environment for the children and allow them to build meaningful relationships. name: Social Innovation and Public Service (SIPS) Fund
description: The Georgetown University Social Innovation and Public Service (SIPS) Fund is a $1.5 million student-run fund that allocates approximately $60,000 in award money every year to help students and alumni start their own social ventures. The mission of SIPS grows out of the Jesuit tradition of service to others.

name: Society of Catholic Students
description: The Society of Catholic Students exists to cultivate Catholic community at Georgetown Law. Our goal is to provide a space where all students can encounter the life-changing love of Jesus Christ and delve deeper into relationship with Him through prayer, fellowship, and the sacraments of the Church.

name: Society of Physics Students
description: Georgetown University's Society of Physics Students is a student-run organization that aims to foster a sense of community among undergraduate students in the department.

name: South Asian Law Students Association
description: The Georgetown University Law Center's South Asian Law Students Association strives to preserve and increase awareness of South Asian heritage at the Law Center and in the legal field through the ideals of cultural and social awareness, diversity and inclusion, and community service.

name: South Asian Society
description: The South Asian Society (SAS) seeks to meet the social, cultural, and educational needs of all Hoyas with an interest in South Asia. SAS proudly celebrates the cultural, religious, and linguistic diversity of South Asia and seeks to raise awareness of South Asian cultures at Georgetown. SAS is committed to building a sense of community among its members and exists to provide a unified voice for South Asian interests on campus. South Asia includes, but is not limited to, the nations of Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, the Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka.

name: Space Law Society
description: The purpose of the Space Law Society (SLS) is to be a leader on campus in the practice of space law. The Space Law Society seeks to provide foundational education and support in the subject matter of space law, increase awareness of current space law issues, and elevate opportunities for students to get involved in the broader space law community and engage with the field at both the domestic and international level.

name: Special Olympics Club
description: The mission of Special Olympics is to provide year-round sports training and athletic competition in a variety of Olympic-type sports for children and adults with intellectual disabilities, giving them continuing opportunities to develop physical fitness, demonstrate courage, experience joy, and participate in a sharing of gifts, skills, and friendship with their families, other Special Olympics athletes, and the community.

name: St. Elizabeths Outreach Program
description: St. Elizabeths Outreach is a club which connects Georgetown students interested in mental health and social justice with volunteer opportunities at St Elizabeths Hospital. The organization hosts weekly visits to the hospital, where volunteers play board games and chat with the individuals in care. Central to the club's mission is a commitment to mental health advocacy and a commitment to the intersection of social justice and healthcare.

name: Statutes & Ladders
description: To provide an accessible and respectful space for all board game lovers, TTRPG explorers, and casual game enjoyers to come together on a regular basis to play games and have fun regardless of any career interest or identity

description: CSJ Student Academic Assistants (SAAs) support social justice, community-engaged, and community-based learning courses, research, and scholarly initiatives taught and led by CSJ-affiliated faculty. When supporting a course, SAAs complete organizational and logistical tasks to support the course professor, students, and community partners, including but not limited to: entering and organizing course data, sending email and text reminders to students, and professionally communicating with community partners via phone and email. name: Student Bar Association
description: The Student Bar Association ("SBA") is composed of the House of Delegates and the Executive Board. The SBA works through a variety of internal and external committees to make positive changes to campus policy, engage with members of the faculty and administration, and host events for the Georgetown Law community. The SBA meets bi-monthly during the academic year, and meetings are open to all students to share suggestions or concerns.

name: Student Centers
description: The mission of Student Centers is to provide a welcoming environment for Georgetown students, faculty, staff, alumni, and visitors and to support programs, activities, and services that promote community, personal growth, lifelong learning, and responsible citizenship in service to others. Student Centers aims to uphold the Jesuit and Catholic Identity of Georgetown University by providing a central meeting place and facility for the community to develop insights through reflection, intellectual inquiry, and creativity. name: Students Advancing Food Equity
description: The mission of Students Advancing Food Equity (SAFE) is to ensure that all Georgetown University community members have the ability and opportunity to access healthy and affordable food.

description: Nationally, Students for Justice in Palestine's work is centered on freedom, justice, and equality for the Palestinian people, particularly as it pertains to Israeli occupation. SJP Nationals believes that all struggles for freedom, justice, and equality are interconnected and that we must embody the principles and ideals we envision for a just society. There are more than 200 chapters at undergraduate and graduate campuses around the country, and Georgetown Law had an active chapter until a few years ago. name: Students of Color Alliance
description: The Student of Color Alliance (SOCA) is a collaborative umbrella organization formed by representatives from the cultural groups on campus. SOCA aims to unite students of color through collaborative programming opportunities, advocacy, and financial support.

description: The Navy ROTC Program was established to develop midshipmen mentally, morally and physically and to imbue them with the highest ideals of duty, and loyalty, and with the core values of honor, courage and commitment in order to commission college graduates as naval and Marine Corps officers. Students of NROTC is an association that supports Midshipmen at Georgetown University to fulfill this mission set forth by the United States Navy, and become the highest quality officers as they can be.

Established in April 2008, TASA is open anyone who is interested in learning more about Taiwan. Our mission is to provide a robust platform for networking, knowledge sharing, and professional growth within the tax law community. We seek to provide a forum that unites Georgetown's students, alumni, faculty, Jesuits, and administrators through a common affinity for the arts and a shared respect for the history, spirit, and intellectual tradition of our University.

description: The Berkley Center for Religion, Peace, and World Affairs seeks a more just and peaceful world by deepening knowledge and solving problems at the intersection of religion and global affairs through research, teaching, and engaging multiple publics. Recognizing the unique and legitimate style of mixed-voice a cappella music, the founders felt there was a need for an arts group at Georgetown which would specialize in this type of performance. As Georgetown University's premier co-ed a cappella group, the Phantoms sing pop, rock, and R&B from a variety of artists at both on and off campus events and are committed to delivering the highest level of performance to spread music and culture.

description: The purpose of The Georgetown Review is to offer a platform for open debate and discussion about important ideas, challenging questions, and other news, serving as an independent outlet for all student and faculty viewpoints on campus, especially conservative and libertarian views, which are traditionally absent or obscured in other campus media outlets. Since then, we have not only diversified our musical repertoire to include today's greatest hits, but we have also extended our reach nationwide, raising funds for charities across the country. Each member of our family has a passion for music and often a personal connection with the organizations we serve.

In addition to a print edition that is published every two weeks, the Voice reports on campus news, leisure, and sports online daily. Our alumni have gone on to work at The New York Times, The Washington Post, The New Yorker, The Atlantic, NPR, NBC, FiveThirtyEight, Sports Illustrated, Vulture, POLITICO, The Huffington Post, and several other news organizations.

name: The Hoya
description: The Hoya is the oldest and largest student newspaper of Georgetown University, serving as the university's newspaper of record since 1920. It is published online daily and every Friday in print during the school year when we are on campus. Each print issue also includes a weekly lifestyle magazine, The Guide. The Hoya also publishes a blog, The Fourth Edition, which provides a lighthearted take on all things Georgetown. description: Established in 2018, Vibe_ is a dance crew at Georgetown University that seeks to connect Eastern and Western culture through dance and social events, stemming from the prospering Korean Pop culture which transcends international borders. With tenets of performance and community and comprised of members from all backgrounds and experience levels, Vibe_ serves as an inclusive and safe environment for all searching for a fun and integrative community that shares a passion for diversity, culture, and dance. description: We, the students at Georgetown University, have established a Vietnamese Student Association that strives to promote awareness of the Vietnamese-American culture, works toward the collective benefit of the Georgetown and Vietnamese American Community, welcomes cultural diversity, advocates for social justice, and raises a voice in global issues affecting the international Vietnamese community. Through our cultural events, we hope to bring a little bit of Vietnam to Georgetown, and through our philanthropic events, a little bit of Georgetown to Vietnam.

name: WGTB Georgetown Radio
description: WGTB is Georgetown University's student-run, internet-streaming campus radio station, serving as Georgetown's central source for music news, reviews, events, and community. Our mission is to be an integral part of the Georgetown undergraduate experience and the Washington community, providing a forum for students to broadcast their ideas, discover new music, and enjoy live performances. Through our on-air programming, online publication, live concerts, and online events, we aspire to help the Georgetown community enjoy and express themselves creatively.

name: What's A Hoya
description: Our mission is to give the individual Hoya the tools and knowledge they need to become better citizens, community members, people, and Hoyas.

description: Women in Faith (WIF) is an interfaith org for all who identify as femme, whether from a specific faith tradition, interfaith background, no faith or undefined. WiF hopes to create a network of solidarity to discuss the intersection of womxn & religion. WiF hopes to fill the need for sustained conversations between women across faith communities that too often aren't given adequate time or space for discussion and reflection. name: Women in Science and Education
description: To raise awareness of gender-specific challenges that exist in science and academia; to encourage and promote spaces for dialogue on working toward solutions to overcome biases in science and academia; and to establish a mentorship network between Georgetown students and the faculty and administration.

name: Women of Color
description: GUWOC is an organization that strives to address the experiences and uplift the voices of women of color at Georgetown. We are especially concerned with the intersection of race and gender and how that translates into the lives and experiences of women of color specifically as we navigate a predominantly white institution. Our organization hosts events and provides resources to create a community of women of color that is rooted in advocacy, support, and love.

name: Women of Color Collective
description: The Women of Color Collective seeks to provide a safe, inclusive and thought provoking space for all who share our support for women of color on Georgetown's law campus and beyond. Through strategic programming that caters to our members' professional and personal development, our organization seeks to bridge the gap between women of color and the opportunities they are often denied on account of their race, class, and gender.

name: Women's Center
description: The Georgetown University Women's Center seeks to create community through a holistic approach that fosters a just and equitable environment for students, faculty, staff, and alumni informed by the Jesuit tradition.

name: Women's Club Basketball
description: To create an atmosphere where we can compete against the best teams in our league, while also maintaining a fun atmosphere where we can grow and enjoy playing the game.

description: Georgetown University Women's Club Soccer Team is established for the purpose of extending the opportunity to the undergraduate females of Georgetown University of participating in a more competitive and more demanding level of soccer than intramurals allows. The Georgetown University Women's Club Soccer Team will compete intercollegiately throughout the area.

name: Women's Legal Alliance
description: Originally an on-campus student organization, the Georgetown Women's Legal Alliance ("WLA") connects individuals who are affiliated with the Law Center and have an interest in women's equality and advancement within the legal profession. WLA welcomes alumni, students, and professors of all gender identities as equals. According to the interests of members, WPE's repertoire varies by semester but always draws from around the world — from traditional North American percussion literature to Afro-Cuban, Latin, African, Eastern, and European styles. name: Ye Domesday Booke
description: GEORGETOWN OFFICIAL YEARBOOK The Georgetown Yearbook (Ye Domesday Booke) has been a pillar of the community since 1901. With this long-standing tradition, the publication has gone through drastic changes throughout the years. In the beginning, the book was commemorated solely towards documenting the graduating class's final year. Throughout the decades, the book went from only pictures to more of a newspaper format to what it is now -- a combination of documenting D.C., Georgetown, and the graduating class's history through articles, photographs, student art, and more.
